title: WhatsApp Business Cloud: Send a Message can’t reply to users with a WhatsApp username (BSUID), no recipient field or API Call module
text: What is your goal? That the user receives the message and the bot can continue the conversation. What is the problem & what have you tried? I use the WhatsApp Business Cloud app with a number connected via Coexistence. More and more of my customers now write using a WhatsApp username. For them, the Watch Events module does not return wa_id; it only returns: contacts .user_id (BSUID, e.g. CO.1419215493729121) contacts .profile.username (e.g. LauraCajica) I need my automation to reply to these users, and I tested the Send a Message module (Receiver field): Receiver = username (LauraCajica or @LauraCajica ): Meta rejects it with error 131009, “phone number format is incorrect, use +1234567890”. Receiver = BSUID (CO.1419215493729121): the module returns a wamid, but the message is not delivered to the user. According to Meta’s documentation, BSUID recipients should be addressed with the recipient field instead of to. The Send a Message module does not expose it, and this app has no “Make an API Call” module, so I can’t send the request manually. My questions: Is there a way to reply to a BSUID with the current modules? Will the module support the recipient field soon? Could a “Make an API Call” module be added to WhatsApp Business Cloud? This blocks automations for any business that uses the official API, because phone numbers are hidden for many users. Thank you! Error messages or input/output bundles no error. 3 posts - 3 participants Read full topic
triage_reason: Make.com user stuck because WhatsApp Business Cloud API lacks a recipient identifier for BSUIDs.

title: New Collborator request form UX is annoying
text: The https://dev.shopify.com/dashboard/129017439/stores/collaborations/new form needs an update as UX was designed 10 years ago most likely. If I want to choose granular permissions, I have to go through 10-20 checkboxes manually, expand each one, and select them. Why cant you make predefined roles available for partner stores? Even if its just preselecting permissions. When there is a mistake in collaborator code all selected checkboxes get whiped out and have to start over! Is this to preventing DDosing requests stores? I’m sure there is a more elegant solution to this then having valid users doing manual checking if they made a mistake or used an expired collaborator code. Why can’t we update an existing request with additional permissions? If I missed any checkbox manually, I need to remove the access, then go through the manual process again with the additional checkbox. Even if the backend doesnt support it, it could just handle the rerequest actions automatically without asking user to do it. This becomes really annoying when you have to do it more than once, and it would be easy to fix in an hour or less and make partner life less miserable. 2 posts - 2 participants Read full topic
triage_reason: Partner frustrated by tedious checkbox UI in Shopify collaborator request form.

title: Request to get Staff ID's through admin or API
text: Our point of sale app allows users to set up conditions. One request is to have a condition based on the staff member. To be able to set this condition up proactively, prior to the store going live - we would want to get a list of the pos staff_id’s. This doesn’t seem to existeither in the admin or api. The staff_id we can access through the api, is for the Shopify parent user ID. In POS, I believe that ID is the user that logged in to the device, not the staff member who has pinned in. The only way we see the pinned in staff_id is if that member completes a sale, or potentially, manually on device. We can then view it in our logs and in reporting. tl;dr what I’m searching for: A way to query the retail staff id’s (not user id’s) that have been set up Or, more staff properties available in the pos session api such as their permission level or tag. That would let us forgo needing this entirely since we could likely filter on that instead. cheers 6 posts - 5 participants Read full topic

title: Investigating Shopify Technical Issues When Pages Are Indexed but Google and AI Visibility Declines
text: I’m researching whether a technical inconsistency can affect how Google and AI search systems discover, interpret and display a Shopify website. My situation is that Google continues to crawl my website, index pages, products are synced and approved within Google Merchant Center and structured data is present. However, my visibility both local or organic have declined. Some AI-generated answers have failed to identify the business accurately or even suggesting it doesn’t exist. I understand that Google Search, local results, and AI search don’t necessarily work the same way, and I’m starting to wonder if shopify as e-commerce affects service based businesses as well. I’m simply trying to determine whether there could be an underlying technical issue that hasn’t been identified. I’m curious whether anyone else has experienced something similar or investigated any of the following: Can a Shopify theme or its customizations interfere with how search engines read or interpret a website, even when pages are indexed? Can structured data be valid but still contain conflicting or incomplete information that affects how a business or its products are understood? Have you encountered issues involving crawler access, robots.txt, JavaScript, or conflicting information within a Shopify website? How would you determine whether the issue is technical rather than simply a change in Google’s rankings or how AI search results are generated? Has anyone experienced something similar and actually identified the cause? If so, what was it? I’m not looking for general SEO advice or recommendations to rewrite content. I’m particularly interested in hearing from people who have encountered these types of issues, how they identified them, and whether correcting them made a measurable difference. 6 posts - 5 participants Read full topic
triage_reason: Merchant investigating technical indexing inconsistencies affecting Google and AI search visibility.

title: Neue Zollregeln in Verbindung mit Drobshipping
text: Hallo in die Runde, ich habe meinen Shop erst im Juli 2026 begonnen, und wurde sogleich von den neuen Zöllen überrascht. Seit Juli müssen ja für Warensendungen aus Drittländern (nicht-EU) unter 150,- € Zölle gezahlt werden, bzw. ab November auch noch Bearbeitungsgebühren. Seit dem suche ich nach einer praktikablen Lösung, um diese Zölle und ggf. Einfuhrumsatzsteuern im Checkout zu berechnen, damit meine Kunden diese nicht bei der Zustellung noch zahlen müssen. Da ich meine Produkte via Print on demand herstellen lasse, handelt es sich wohl um sogenanntes Drobshipping!? Mein Hersteller produziert weltweit, und würde auch weltweit liefern. Inzwischen habe ich schon herausgefunden, das es sogenannte DDP Label/Etiketten gibt, aber mein Print on demand Lieferant bietet diese Möglichkeit nicht für Deutschland an. Außerdem erscheint es mir auch unlogisch, da die Bestellung ja erst nach dem Checkout an den Lieferanten geht, und erst dann erfolgt die Feststellung aus welchem Land wohin geliefert wird. Ich hoffe, ich habe das einigermaßen verständlich erklärt!? Vielleicht stehe ich bei diesem Thema auch zu sehr auf dem Schlauch… aber, ich kann mir nicht vorstellen, das es nicht irgendwie doch eine technische Lösung, oder eine App gibt, die diese Berechnung im Checkout durchführt. Außerdem kann ich es mir kaum vorstellen, das seit dem Massenhaft Pakete zugestellt werden, und die Zusteller Zoll und Einfuhrumsatzsteuer kassieren. Gibt es hier jemanden der ein ähnliches Problem hat oder hatte? Wie könnte man das lösen? Oder ist meine oben erwähnte logische Reihenfolge schon die Erklärung, und es gibt aktuell noch keine Lösung? Dann würde mich noch interessieren, sofern es eine Lösung gibt, wie und wo macht dann die Zollmeldung oder kann man auch den Zoll und die Bearbeitungsgebühr via IOSS melden? Ich freue mich auf Eure Antworten. Grüße Melanie 3 posts - 3 participants Read full topic
triage_reason: Dropshipper struggling to calculate and report new EU customs duties and handling fees at checkout.
